title: Show a machine as degraded when helpers aren't running
body:
### Feature request description

A podman machine runs Podman in a VM but needs some extra processes (helpers), such as gvproxy, to be fully operational. A machine started manually (with `wsl -d` rather than `podman machine start` for example) shows as runnning (because a Podman service is running inside the guest) but `podman run` may not work if the helpers aren't running.

c.f. this discussion https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29837#pullrequestreview-5738066281

### Suggest potential solution

Introduce a new `Degraded` [machine state](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/7f9afb85692947c063cc02416ad60ef7096d7037/pkg/machine/define/state.go) to be returned by [`VMProvider.State()`](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/7f9afb85692947c063cc02416ad60ef7096d7037/pkg/machine/vmconfigs/config.go#L73) when the Podman service is healthy but helpers (gvproxy, win-sshproxy, user-mode-networking wsl distrib) aren't. 

Then carefully review the different machine commands that use [`VMProvider.State()`](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/7f9afb85692947c063cc02416ad60ef7096d7037/pkg/machine/vmconfigs/config.go#L73) and update the behavior for when it returns `Degraded`.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Introduce a new `Helpers.State()` instead of modifying existing `VMProvider.State()`.
